### 2. Customer FAQ (what people really asked, and the answer to give)

Answers are written in Nxeon voice and can be pasted. Source ticket/chat in brackets.

**Where do I find / change my server password?** Settings tab, "Server password" (General group). Valheim needs at least 5 characters and the password must not be contained in the world name. Saving restarts the server. [T1, T7, LC7]

**Checkout says a server password is required but I can't see the field.** This was a real checkout bug on 2026-09-16 (the password field was missing from the deploy form for the 4 GB plan). Staff workaround used: deployed manually after the customer topped up the wallet. If it recurs, treat as a bug (spawn a task), deploy by hand, and do NOT tell the customer to "just type password" in the form. The password is editable afterwards in Settings. [T7, LC7]

**How do I connect?** Valheim > Join Game > Join by IP > `<server address>:<game port>` exactly as shown on the server Overview (the port is NOT 2456 on NAT nodes), then the server password. Consoles and crossplay: see Playbook 9. [T1, T15]

**Failed to connect, no password prompt.** Almost always ports/addressing/boot time/mod mismatch: run Playbook 1. [T1, T12, T15]

**Why is my ping high?** Distance to the server region. A server can be moved to another region (e.g. Singapore for Southeast Asia): staff-run, 30-45 min of downtime, new address, same password, world carried over. Never promise a time window beyond that range; Singapore capacity can mean a new node first. [T1, T15]

**Can I move my server to another region?** Yes, via support (Section 6, "Moving a server"). Ask for the world folder first if they have one newer than ours. [T1, T15, LC15]

**How do I upload my own world?** Files tab -> upload the **whole world folder** (new Valheim 1.0 saves are a folder named after the world containing `_main.N.db2`, `.fwl2` and `.chunk` files) into `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/`, then set the World name in Settings to exactly that folder name (changing the name creates/loads that world; old worlds stay on disk). Old-style single files are `<World>.db` + `<World>.fwl`. If upload by folder is not available to the customer yet, they zip it and staff extract it. Staff can also attach it by hand. [T15, LC15]

**Can I upload mods myself?** Yes: Files tab -> `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`. The server type must be BepInEx. See Section 4 for the zip rule. [T15]

**How do I extract a zip in the file manager?** Extract-on-server and folder upload are merged to main (commits `ca30a05922`, `a6201db7ed`); confirm they are deployed before telling a customer the button exists (see Section 7). Until then staff extract it over SSH. [T15]

**I installed a mod and nobody can join / version incompatible.** Every player must have the same gameplay mods at the same version as the server. Playbook 5. [T2, T12]

**Can you install ValheimPlus?** Not recommended: marked deprecated/unmaintained on Thunderstore after the 1.0 update (Sept 11). It also requires the matching client mod. Offer alternatives (e.g. MaxPlayerCount, BetterNetworking). The catalog entry still exists (`valheimplus-grantapher`): do not install it for a customer without telling them about the client requirement. [T2, T12]

**Can I get 20 players on the 4 GB plan?** The plan's slot count is 10. Staff installed MaxPlayerCount (Azumatt) for a customer; its default doubles vanilla's limit (to 20), but RAM headroom is the real constraint on the 4 GB plan: recommend the 8 GB plan for 20 players. Everyone needs no client install for MaxPlayerCount? UNVERIFIED (server-side behaviour; confirm against the mod's Thunderstore page before promising). [T2]

**Where is the in-game console / how do I get admin?** Playbook 6. [T4, LC4, LC15]

**Can you turn raids off / change death penalty / portals?** Yes, Settings tab -> World group: Raid frequency, Death penalty, Portal restrictions, and presets. Each save restarts the server. [T5, LC4]

**My mod disappeared after a Valheim update.** A Steam update reset the mod loader; restart the server (files are intact). Playbook 4. [T11]

**Crossplay: my PS5 friend can't join.** Playbook 9. The answer changed during the ticket: do not assert a flat "PlayStation is impossible" without checking the current game version (see Playbook 9). [T6]

**How do I see who has been on the server?** Players tab: online count (real, from the server log) and a known-players list with last-seen times; leave times are approximate. [T10]

**The console shows "1.82 GiB is not enough memory" on my 4 GB plan.** The line comes from the container image's own check and is shown when the guest sees less RAM than the plan. A 4 GB plan should show about 3.8 GB; ~1.8 GB means the VM was squeezed (Playbook 8 ballooning). Do not answer "the OS takes the rest": that was the Sept 17 answer and the real cause (balloon floor 2048) was only found on 2026-10-01. [T8]

**Can I change the world name?** Yes, but a new name means a new world (the old one stays on disk and returns if you set the old name back). Some names crash world generation: "terraheim" did on 2026-09-08 (UNVERIFIED as an engine bug; it was the observed behaviour and it was worked around with a new name). [T1]

**Is there a free Valheim server?** A community server is built but dormant until an owner sets it LIVE (`/free-valheim-server`, `/admin/free-servers`); until then answer "not yet". Free Minecraft exists. [PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md]

**Which games / prices?** Valheim $9.99 (4 GB, 10 players) and $16.99 (8 GB, 20 players) per month. The chat bot wrongly said "we have no 4 GB Valheim tier" on Sept 24 (LC9, LC11): its plan list (`lib/kb-plans.ts`) only carries the 8 GB plan. Correct that if you see it.

### 3. Troubleshooting playbooks

Conventions: run server-side commands on the game VM over SSH (or the admin "Ops" console). Container name is `valheim`. Node-side commands run on the Proxmox node hosting the VM. Never restart or recreate a customer's container without telling them: it disconnects players.

#### Playbook 1: Players cannot connect ("Failed to connect")

Symptom: Join IP fails with no password prompt, or "Incompatible version", or the server shows online but nobody can join. (Builds on the existing runbook above.)

Checks, in order (about 5 minutes):
1. **Is it really up?** `docker ps` shows `valheim` Up; `docker logs --tail 200 valheim | grep -n "Game server connected"` and confirm that line is newer than `docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' valheim`. After any restart/reboot allow ~3 min with many mods (23 mods = ~3 min).
2. **Right address and port?** Overview shows the public IP and the public game port for this server. Customers often use 2456, an old port from before a move, or the query port. Ask them to paste exactly what they typed into the Join IP box.
3. **Reachable from outside?** A2S query goes to the QUERY port = game port + 1 (public N+1). From any machine outside the node:
   `python3 -c "import socket;s=socket.socket(2,2);s.settimeout(4);s.sendto(b'\xff\xff\xff\xffTSource Engine Query\x00',('<ip>',<N+1>));print(s.recvfrom(2048)[0][:60])"`. A reply containing the server name = good. A reply starting with byte `A` is a challenge = still success. No reply = port/firewall/server down. The game port N itself does not answer A2S.
4. **Do their packets arrive?** On the node: `iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD_<nodeN> -v -n | grep dpt:<port>`; counters should climb while the customer retries. No movement = they are not sending to this IP:port (wrong address, VPN, ISP, local firewall).
5. **Three consecutive ports?** Public N, N+1, N+2 must forward to 2456, 2457, 2458 UDP (PortForward rows + iptables). Non-consecutive public ports (seen 2026-10-01: 20089/20004/20005) break the Steam handshake: fix by re-allocating consecutively. Missing 2457/2458 entirely was the 2026-09-08 cause (T1) and is now auto-created at provision.
6. **Guest memory sane?** `free -m` total must match the plan (4 GB plan ~3.8 GB). ~1.8 GB means ballooning: `qm config <vmid> | grep balloon` on the node; fix `qm set <vmid> --balloon 0` then a COLD reboot (a live `balloon` monitor command is undone by pvestatd).
7. **Mod parity?** `ls /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`. Compare to the customer's client list; any gameplay mod missing/different version = refusal (Playbook 5).
8. **Customer-side network test** (PowerShell, query port; the one used in chat T15):
   `$u = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.UdpClient; $u.Connect("<ip>",<N+1>); $b=[byte[]](0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff)+[Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes("TSource Engine Query`0"); $u.Send($b,$b.Length) | Out-Null; $u.Client.ReceiveTimeout=4000; try { $ep=New-Object Net.IPEndPoint([Net.IPAddress]::Any,0); [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($u.Receive([ref]$ep)) } catch { "no reply" }`. Gibberish containing the server name or a leading `A` = their network reaches us. "no reply" = their ISP/VPN/firewall or wrong address. NOTE the backtick-zero must survive copy/paste; in T15 a version without the backtick was sent and a plain "0" is not a NUL byte.
9. **Restart the client.** On 2026-10-01 the customer connected after restarting the Valheim client: Steam networking can cache a failed session.

Fix: correct the address; re-forward ports consecutively; `--balloon 0` + cold reboot; remove/align mods; wait out the boot.
Tell the customer: the server is healthy on our side (say what you verified), give the exact address:port, ask them to restart their game and retry; if still failing ask for a screenshot of the Join box + error and their mod list.

#### Playbook 2: Server crashes / restarts / will not start

Checks:
- `docker ps -a`, `docker logs --tail 300 valheim`, `journalctl -u valheim* --no-pager -n 100` (the control layer resolves a unit via hints `valheim`, `valheim-server`).
- BepInEx errors: `grep -i -E "error|exception|could not" /opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/LogOutput.log | tail -50`.
- Crash during world creation every time: a specific world name (T1 "terraheim"). Set another world name in Settings (this makes a NEW world; tell the customer).
- Password under 5 chars or containing the world name: Valheim refuses to start. Fix in Settings.
- RAM: `free -m`, `docker stats --no-stream valheim`, OOM in `dmesg | grep -i oom`.
- A mod install/BepInEx toggle triggers a restart by design (T2: "BetterNetworking tripped a quick reboot"). Tell customers up front that installs restart the server.
- First-boot BepInEx download (switching vanilla -> bepinex) can take several minutes.
Fix: remove the offending plugin folder from `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins` (move it aside, do not delete), `docker restart valheim`; or revert the setting.
Tell the customer: what restarted and why, that the world is intact (verify `ls /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local`), and what to do next.

#### Playbook 3: World missing / switched / reverted (see the 2026-09-11 incident, T3)

Symptom: "all our progress vanished" after saving a setting, restarting or pressing the update button; or the server returned an older world.
Facts: (1) a Settings-save bug used to re-apply the stored `world` value and silently switch the live world; fixed on main in commit `8f6066be2e` ("fix Valheim world-switch bug", `applyValheim` now only changes `WORLD_NAME` when it differs from the running container). Deployment of that commit to prod: UNVERIFIED here, confirm. (2) The old world is NOT deleted: it is still in `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local`. (3) The same incident also hit the self-service "restore from backup" with a false identity alarm (`net0 expected virtio, VM reports virtio=...`): fixed in the same commit; do not use self-service restore on an affected server until confirmed deployed.
Checks:
- `docker inspect valheim --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -E "WORLD_NAME|SERVER_ARGS"` (the world being run) and `grep -E "WORLD_NAME" /root/valheim.env`.
- `ls -la --time=birth /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/` and `ls -lt` to see which worlds exist and which was written last. The one with the newest modification time and the most data is the one players have been playing on.
- Compare with the customer's own account of which world has their latest progress BEFORE switching anything (in T3 staff restored the old world and wiped the customer's second progress: ask, do not assume).
- Remember a world is a folder with `_main.N.db2`, `.fwl2`, `.chunk` files (1.0) or a `.db` + `.fwl` pair (old).
Fix: set Settings > World name to the exact name of the correct world (or edit `WORLD_NAME` in `/root/valheim.env` and recreate via the dashboard, not by hand, so the platform stays in sync), then confirm in the log that the intended world loaded. Before any change, copy the world folder: `cp -a /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local /root/worlds_local.$(date +%F-%H%M)`.
Tell the customer: which world is running now, that no world was deleted, what caused it, and that a rename always starts a new world.

#### Playbook 4: Mods not loading / "mod disappeared"

Checks:
- Server type must be `bepinex` (Settings). On `vanilla` nothing loads (2 of 4 live servers were vanilla on 2026-10-01).
- Folder layout: DLLs under `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/<Author-Mod>/` (BepInEx loads recursively). The image copies this folder into the live BepInEx dir at container start, so changes need a restart.
- `grep -i "loading \[" /opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/LogOutput.log` lists what actually loaded; compare with the folder.
- After a Valheim Steam update the loader can be reset: the files are intact but not loaded. Fix: restart the server (T11, twice in one day: a second update the same day required a second restart).
- Missing dependency (Jotunn, other BepInEx libs): log shows missing reference / type load exceptions. Install the dependency into its own plugin folder.
- Mods built for an older game build can crash or silently fail after 1.0 (T15 customer: "some mods might be for older versions").
- Packages with `patchers/`, `core/`, `monomod/` folders are refused by the one-click installer: the image does not sync those preloader folders from `/config`.
Fix: restart; install missing deps; remove incompatible mods; switch to `bepinex` type.
Tell the customer: the files are safe, a game update reset the loader, a restart reloads them; mention it can recur after the next Valheim update.

#### Playbook 5: Version / mod mismatch ("Incompatible version", join refused after a mod install)

Facts: a server marked modded requires every gameplay mod on every client at the same version (ValheimPlus case, T12). Server-only/cosmetic-free mods are fine without client install; client-side-only mods are not catalogued for servers.
Checks: list server plugins (`ls /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`) and each manifest version (`cat .../<Mod>/manifest.json` where present); ask for the player's r2modman/Thunderstore profile export or screenshot. Also check the base game version: the game builds must match (the server self-updates only when idle; players may be a build ahead/behind after a patch day: A2S EDF keywords `g=1.0.xx` shows the server build).
Fix: align versions (players install the same mod versions) or remove the mod server-side (note that removal restarts the server). Install via the dashboard Mods tab where possible so versions are the newest and dependencies are included.
Tell the customer: the exact mod names/versions required on every PC, or that we removed the mod and they can join again.

#### Playbook 6: Console / admin / devcommands

Facts: vanilla Valheim never gives a remote admin cheat access on a real dedicated server (the gate `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()` is host-only), so `devcommands` fails even for admins. The third-party "Server devcommands" mod crashed on the current game build (HarmonyException in `Awake()`, 2026-09-09). Nxeon's own plugin (`NxeonDevAdmin`) does the one needed thing: lets a player in `adminlist.txt` use devcommands. It is mounted automatically on every `bepinex` server. It is NOT active on `vanilla` servers.
Steps for the customer: (1) server type = BepInEx (Settings; world is kept); (2) find their Steam64 ID (17 digits, steamid.io); (3) Files tab: edit `/opt/valheim/config/adminlist.txt` and add the ID **on its own line, with a trailing newline**; or enter it in Settings > "Admin SteamIDs" (`ADMINLIST_IDS`, space-separated; the image writes the file). (4) Restart the server; (5) join and press F5 to open the console, then `devcommands`.
Checks if it still fails: file ends with a newline and has no stray characters (LC4: a missing newline was found); `adminlist.txt` format accepted by the image is a bare SteamID64 per line (the Platform-prefixed `Steam_<id>` form appears in the 2026-09-20 notes: UNVERIFIED which the current image prefers, try the bare form first); `ls /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/nxeon-dev-admin` exists; `grep -i NxeonDevAdmin /opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/LogOutput.log` shows it loaded; confirm the third-party "Server devcommands" mod is NOT installed alongside it (T-LC4: uninstall it). Achievements restore after the cheat-flag patch: each player runs the patch-note command individually (`yesiuseddevcommandsbutiwantmyachievementsanyway`); admin-list membership does not apply it server-wide (T4).
Server log is visible in the dashboard Console tab; there is no command box for Valheim.
Tell the customer: the steps above, and that being on the admin list grants console access only.

#### Playbook 7: Password rules

- Required, minimum 5 characters, must not be contained in the world name (Valheim refuses to start otherwise). Stored as `SERVER_PASS` in `/root/valheim.env`.
- Changing it recreates the container (restart). Tell players the new password.
- Historic: before 2026-09-08 every server shared the catalog default `changeme12` and the field was not visible. Any server older than that may still run it: check `grep SERVER_PASS /root/valheim.env` on old servers (UNVERIFIED how many remain) and recommend a change. Do not paste passwords into tickets.
- A "SSH password" is a different thing (VM login, Overview > SSH, "Reset password" button). T1 lost time to this confusion: confirm which one the customer means.

#### Playbook 8: Performance / memory / ballooning

- Valheim is mostly single-thread-bound; RAM scales with explored world and mods. Recommendation basis: `lib/game-player-recommend.ts` (about 410 MB per player over base: ESTIMATE, not measured).
- `free -m`; `docker stats --no-stream valheim`; compare to plan. 4 GB plan with ~23 mods booted and ran, but it is tight; recommend 8 GB for heavy mod lists or 20 players.
- Ballooning: new VMs get a balloon floor of 50% (`worker/index.ts` `balloonFloorMB`, min 1024); on a 4 GB plan that is 2048. On a busy node Proxmox can squeeze the guest to ~1.8 GB (`1.82 GiB is not enough memory` in the log, T8; confirmed again 2026-10-01). Fix: on the node `qm set <vmid> --balloon 0` and cold reboot (stop + start, not guest reboot-only). Verify with `free -m` inside the guest.
- High ping: region (Playbook in FAQ). Valheim tolerates up to ~100 ms (PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md); 276 ms from Philippines to Germany was the T1 case.
- Lag with BetterNetworking-type mods is normally an improvement; staff recommended it (T2).

#### Playbook 9: Crossplay / consoles

- Setting: Settings > Crossplay (`CROSSPLAY=true`). Before 2026-09-15 the setting was saved but never applied to the container (fixed in `applyValheim`); on older servers check `docker inspect valheim | grep CROSSPLAY` shows `CROSSPLAY=true`.
- Crossplay switches Steam matchmaking to PlayFab so Xbox / Microsoft Store (and, per the T6 outcome, PlayStation) clients can join. In T6 staff first said PlayStation is excluded, then the customer found an official statement and the PS5 player did join. Treat console support as supported when `CROSSPLAY=true`, and verify the current platform list against Iron Gate's current docs before promising a specific platform: UNVERIFIED.
- Consoles cannot type an IP. Console players find servers by NAME in the in-game server list; so the server must be listed (community/public listing) and the exact name given. Ask what exactly the console player enters (T6). Server name is `SERVER_NAME` (default "Nxeon" at provision; the Settings schema for Valheim has no server-name field: UNVERIFIED how the customer renames it today, see Section 7).
- A PC/Steam client joins crossplay servers by the same Join IP flow.

#### Playbook 10: Backups and restore

Three different things, do not mix them up:
1. **Image auto-backups (in-game world zips):** the `lloesche/valheim-server` image archives worlds to `/opt/valheim/config/backups/` (zip files, automatic, old ones pruned). Schedule/retention defaults are the image's own (README memory: hourly, ~3 days: UNVERIFIED, read `docker exec valheim env | grep BACKUP`). To restore one: stop the server (`docker stop valheim`), copy the current world folder aside, unzip the archive into `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/` (zips contain the world files), start, confirm in the log.
2. **Dashboard "Backups" tab / world backup job (`GAME_BACKUP`):** archives the located world dir to `/var/backups/nxeon-game/valheim-<timestamp>.tar.gz`. The directory search list for Valheim does not include `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local` (see Section 7): on current Docker-based servers this job may report "Could not locate the world/save directory": UNVERIFIED live, test before relying on it.
3. **VM backups (vzdump):** platform disaster recovery and the customer's "restore from backup" on the server page. A false identity alarm that left VMs powered off was fixed in `8f6066be2e` (confirm deployed). Until you have confirmed that, do restores by hand and tell the customer.
Always copy the live world folder before any restore: a world restore overwrites progress made since the backup (T3 lesson).

### 4. Mods guide

How installs work
- **One-click (Mods & Plugins tab / NX Labs catalog, ~1.2k Thunderstore Valheim packages):** `lib/mods/installers/valheim.ts`. Requires server type `bepinex` (else the panel says to switch in Settings; the world is kept). Resolves dependencies from the package's own declared list (max depth 6, max 40 packages), never installs BepInExPack (the image provides BepInEx), refuses packages needing `patchers/core/monomod`, skips `config/` defaults, places files in `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/<Author-Name>/`, records state, supports update/disable/enable/uninstall, then a restart is required to load. Catalog quality gate: non-deprecated, server-side capable, > 1,000 downloads (`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` NX Labs section).
- **Legacy path** (`worker/game-mods.ts` `installModReal`, unzips into `nxeon-<slug>/`) is only used if the engine path is off; the 2026-09-20 note that it never restarts the server applies to that path only.
- **Customer uploads (Files tab):** Thunderstore zips and loose DLLs into `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/`.

The zip rule (verified 2026-10-01, T15 with 23 mods)
1. Thunderstore downloads often bundle several versions: extract **only the newest version**.
2. Put each mod in `plugins/<Author-Mod>/` (a plain DLL can sit loose or in its own folder).
3. **Never extract the BepInExPack zip**: the container already has BepInEx and a second copy breaks loading.
4. Restart afterwards and check `LogOutput.log` for the load lines.

Compatibility traps
- Client parity: gameplay mods must match on every client (Playbook 5). Server-side-only mods (e.g. MaxPlayerCount, BetterNetworking: UNVERIFIED whether each requires a client copy; BetterNetworking is normally installed on both sides, check its Thunderstore page) may not.
- Game updates (1.0 on 2026-09-09 and following patches) break old mods: ValheimPlus is deprecated; many older mod lists in customer zips were for pre-1.0 builds.
- Dependencies: Jotunn (`ValheimModding-Jotunn`) and similar BepInEx library mods must be present for content mods; the one-click installer adds declared dependencies, manual uploads do not.
- Do not combine "Server devcommands" (third-party, crashes on current build) with Nxeon's own NxeonDevAdmin.
- RCON mods exist (`rcon` by AviiNL, `Rcon Commands`): the possible route to real kick/ban is documented in the 2026-09-20 DOCUMENTATION entry and is untested.
- Memory expectations: 23 mods ran on the 4 GB plan but with a ~3 min boot and little headroom; per-player RAM estimate ~410 MB (`lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, estimate). Large mod lists or 20 players: 8 GB plan.
- A mod installed does restart the server (T2). Warn first.

### 5. World management

- **Format (Valheim 1.0):** each world is a folder `worlds_local/<WorldName>/` with `_main.N.db2`, `.fwl2`, and `.chunk` files. Older worlds are `<WorldName>.db` + `.fwl` (+ `_backup_*`). Upload/restore the folder intact; a partial copy (only the db2) will not load. Characters live on each player's PC, not the server.
- **Upload a world:** stop nothing needed if uploading a NEW name; upload folder to `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/`, set Settings > World name to the folder name. Overwriting the currently running world while the server runs is unsafe: stop the server first (staff did this by hand in T15, the customer first uploaded to `/opt/` and staff moved it).
- **Move to another region/node:** Section 6.
- **Backups:** Playbook 10.
- **Presets and modifiers:** Settings > World. `preset` plus per-modifier overrides (`deathpenalty`, `portals`, `raids`); overrides win over the preset. Equivalent to the in-game `-modifier deathpenalty casual -modifier portals casual` requested in LC4. Preset list: normal, casual, easy, hard, hardcore, immersive, hammer (creative). Changing any of them restarts the server; the world data is not reset by modifiers.
- **Seed/new world:** a new world name generates a new world; the old files stay.

### 6. Operations / admin cheat-sheet

Where things are in /admin
- Game servers: `/admin/games`. Server detail/Ops console: `/admin/ops` (diagnose, IP ops, fleet ops, job queue, customer ops). Tickets/chats: admin support area. Community (free) servers: `/admin/free-servers` (area `fleet`). NX Labs: `/admin/nxlabs`.
- Worker jobs relevant to Valheim (systemd `nxeon-worker`; do not restart it): `PROVISION`, `GAME_POWER`, `GAME_CONFIG_APPLY` (settings -> container recreate), `GAME_MOD_SYNC`, `GAME_BACKUP`, `GAME_REINSTALL`, `GAME_UPDATE`, `SYNC_FORWARDS`, `BACKUP_RESTORE`, plus the ~60 s log player-tracking sweep (`logPlayerTrackingSweep`). Job names as seen in code (`lib/actions-game-control.ts`, `worker/index.ts`): check the Ops job queue for exact current types.
- Power start window: 180 s for Valheim (`powerStartTimeoutMs`); UI start grace is 6 min (`lib/game-runtime.ts`).

Moving a server between regions/nodes (T1, T15; staff-run, 30-45 min downtime)
1. Tell the customer the downtime and get consent; ask for any newer world folder (upload to the Files tab or a zip). Do not start the move until the world files are in.
2. Re-provision the same plan on the target node (brand-new VMID, never reuse one, check all 5 nodes; Singapore may need a new node first).
3. Restore world files into `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/` on the new VM (whole folder), copy `adminlist.txt` and the plugins folder, and carry over `/root/valheim.env` values (SERVER_PASS, WORLD_NAME, BEPINEX, CROSSPLAY, SERVER_ARGS) so the password and world stay the same. In T15 the SSH password was not carried over: tell the customer to press "Reset password" if SSH login fails.
4. Verify: log has `Game server connected`, A2S answers on N+1, ports are consecutive (Playbook 1 step 5). Then give the new address (the port changes!) and retire the old VM per policy.
5. Update customer: new `IP:port`, same server password, world loaded.

Gotchas to check on every move or reboot
- **Consecutive port block:** the allocator hands out one public port per rule, so N, N+1, N+2 are not guaranteed (Section 7).
- **Ballooning:** `qm set <vmid> --balloon 0` + cold reboot on 4 GB plans if the guest sees ~1.8 GB.
- **Hairpin/firewall** and node NAT: a VM cannot reach nxeon.cloud unless the firewall hairpin fix is in place (separate entry in this document).
- Never experiment on the customer's live container; copy files first.

Free public Valheim server (dormant until owner action)
- Plan, abuse model and runbook: `docs/PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md`. One shared server, password published and rotated weekly, unlisted (`SERVER_PUBLIC=0`), daily backups kept 7 days, memory limit 4 GB / 2 CPU. Installer and day-2 tool inside the VM: `scripts/provision-public-valheim.sh` (`install`, `status`, `rotate-password`, `backup-now`, `ban`, `update`, `health`). Platform probe: `scripts/probe-free-public-servers.ts`. Marketing page `/free-valheim-server` 404s unless a row is LIVE. The script has never been run on a real VM and its image cron variable names are from memory of the README (UNVERIFIED); confirm in `docker logs` on first boot.

### 8. Customer reply templates

Keep them short, no internal jargon, no provider names, no invented timings. Replace `<...>`. Never send a ticket reply without the owner's sign-off rule for this team being met.

1. **Can't connect (first reply)**
   "Thanks for flagging this. Your server is running on our side. Please join with <ip>:<port> (Join by IP) and the server password from your Settings tab, and restart your Valheim game before trying again, as that clears a cached failed connection. If it still fails, send us a screenshot of the Join box with the error, and the list of mods you have installed on your PC, and we'll dig in right away."

2. **Version mismatch / mod parity**
   "Valheim only lets players in when their mods match the server exactly. Your server runs: <mod list with versions>. Every player needs the same mods at the same versions. If you'd rather not ask everyone to install them, tell us and we'll remove the mod on the server so everyone can join again. Note that adding or removing a mod restarts the server for a minute or two."

3. **Mod disappeared after a game update**
   "A Valheim update reset the mod loader on your server. Your mod files are safe, the server just needs a restart to load them again. Shall we restart now? Players online will be disconnected briefly. This can happen again after the next Valheim update, and a restart fixes it each time."

4. **World missing / switched**
   "We checked your server directly. Your world files are all still saved. The server was loading <current world>, and your <other world> is also still on disk. Tell us which one holds the progress you want and we'll switch to it safely, after taking a copy of both first. We won't change anything until you confirm."

   "To use the in-game console: 1) Find your Steam64 ID (17 digits, steamid.io shows it from your profile link). 2) In your server's Files tab open /opt/valheim/config/adminlist.txt and add the ID on its own line, then save. 3) Restart the server from the dashboard. 4) Join and press F5.    "Open your server's Files tab. Worlds go in /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local (upload the whole world folder, not just one file), then set the World name in Settings to the folder name. ### 3. Troubleshooting playbooks

Conventions: run server-side commands on the game VM over SSH (or the admin "Ops" console). Container name is `valheim`. Node-side commands run on the Proxmox node hosting the VM. Never restart or recreate a customer's container without telling them: it disconnects players.

#### Playbook 1: Players cannot connect ("Failed to connect")

Symptom: Join IP fails with no password prompt, or "Incompatible version", or the server shows online but nobody can join. (Builds on the existing runbook above.)

Checks, in order (about 5 minutes):
1. **Is it really up?** `docker ps` shows `valheim` Up; `docker logs --tail 200 valheim | grep -n "Game server connected"` and confirm that line is newer than `docker inspect -f '{{.State.StartedAt}}' valheim`. After any restart/reboot allow ~3 min with many mods (23 mods = ~3 min).
2. **Right address and port?** Overview shows the public IP and the public game port for this server. Customers often use 2456, an old port from before a move, or the query port. Ask them to paste exactly what they typed into the Join IP box.
3. **Reachable from outside?** A2S query goes to the QUERY port = game port + 1 (public N+1). From any machine outside the node:
   `python3 -c "import socket;s=socket.socket(2,2);s.settimeout(4);s.sendto(b'\xff\xff\xff\xffTSource Engine Query\x00',('<ip>',<N+1>));print(s.recvfrom(2048)[0][:60])"`. A reply containing the server name = good. A reply starting with byte `A` is a challenge = still success. No reply = port/firewall/server down. The game port N itself does not answer A2S.
4. **Do their packets arrive?** On the node: `iptables -t nat -L NXEON_FWD_<nodeN> -v -n | grep dpt:<port>`; counters should climb while the customer retries. No movement = they are not sending to this IP:port (wrong address, VPN, ISP, local firewall).
5. **Three consecutive ports?** Public N, N+1, N+2 must forward to 2456, 2457, 2458 UDP (PortForward rows + iptables). Non-consecutive public ports (seen 2026-10-01: 20089/20004/20005) break the Steam handshake: fix by re-allocating consecutively. Missing 2457/2458 entirely was the 2026-09-08 cause (T1) and is now auto-created at provision.
6. **Guest memory sane?** `free -m` total must match the plan (4 GB plan ~3.8 GB). ~1.8 GB means ballooning: `qm config <vmid> | grep balloon` on the node; fix `qm set <vmid> --balloon 0` then a COLD reboot (a live `balloon` monitor command is undone by pvestatd).
7. **Mod parity?** `ls /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`. Compare to the customer's client list; any gameplay mod missing/different version = refusal (Playbook 5).
8. **Customer-side network test** (PowerShell, query port; the one used in chat T15):
   `$u = New-Object System.Net.Sockets.UdpClient; $u.Connect("<ip>",<N+1>); $b=[byte[]](0xff,0xff,0xff,0xff)+[Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes("TSource Engine Query`0"); $u.Send($b,$b.Length) | Out-Null; $u.Client.ReceiveTimeout=4000; try { $ep=New-Object Net.IPEndPoint([Net.IPAddress]::Any,0); [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetString($u.Receive([ref]$ep)) } catch { "no reply" }`. Gibberish containing the server name or a leading `A` = their network reaches us. "no reply" = their ISP/VPN/firewall or wrong address. NOTE the backtick-zero must survive copy/paste; in T15 a version without the backtick was sent and a plain "0" is not a NUL byte.
9. **Restart the client.** On 2026-10-01 the customer connected after restarting the Valheim client: Steam networking can cache a failed session.

Fix: correct the address; re-forward ports consecutively; `--balloon 0` + cold reboot; remove/align mods; wait out the boot.
Tell the customer: the server is healthy on our side (say what you verified), give the exact address:port, ask them to restart their game and retry; if still failing ask for a screenshot of the Join box + error and their mod list.

#### Playbook 2: Server crashes / restarts / will not start

Checks:
- `docker ps -a`, `docker logs --tail 300 valheim`, `journalctl -u valheim* --no-pager -n 100` (the control layer resolves a unit via hints `valheim`, `valheim-server`).
- BepInEx errors: `grep -i -E "error|exception|could not" /opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/LogOutput.log | tail -50`.
- Crash during world creation every time: a specific world name (T1 "terraheim"). Set another world name in Settings (this makes a NEW world; tell the customer).
- Password under 5 chars or containing the world name: Valheim refuses to start. Fix in Settings.
- RAM: `free -m`, `docker stats --no-stream valheim`, OOM in `dmesg | grep -i oom`.
- A mod install/BepInEx toggle triggers a restart by design (T2: "BetterNetworking tripped a quick reboot"). Tell customers up front that installs restart the server.
- First-boot BepInEx download (switching vanilla -> bepinex) can take several minutes.
Fix: remove the offending plugin folder from `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins` (move it aside, do not delete), `docker restart valheim`; or revert the setting.
Tell the customer: what restarted and why, that the world is intact (verify `ls /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local`), and what to do next.

#### Playbook 3: World missing / switched / reverted (see the 2026-09-11 incident, T3)

Symptom: "all our progress vanished" after saving a setting, restarting or pressing the update button; or the server returned an older world.
Facts: (1) a Settings-save bug used to re-apply the stored `world` value and silently switch the live world; fixed on main in commit `8f6066be2e` ("fix Valheim world-switch bug", `applyValheim` now only changes `WORLD_NAME` when it differs from the running container). Deployment of that commit to prod: UNVERIFIED here, confirm. (2) The old world is NOT deleted: it is still in `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local`. (3) The same incident also hit the self-service "restore from backup" with a false identity alarm (`net0 expected virtio, VM reports virtio=...`): fixed in the same commit; do not use self-service restore on an affected server until confirmed deployed.
Checks:
- `docker inspect valheim --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' | grep -E "WORLD_NAME|SERVER_ARGS"` (the world being run) and `grep -E "WORLD_NAME" /root/valheim.env`.
- `ls -la --time=birth /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/` and `ls -lt` to see which worlds exist and which was written last. The one with the newest modification time and the most data is the one players have been playing on.
- Compare with the customer's own account of which world has their latest progress BEFORE switching anything (in T3 staff restored the old world and wiped the customer's second progress: ask, do not assume).
- Remember a world is a folder with `_main.N.db2`, `.fwl2`, `.chunk` files (1.0) or a `.db` + `.fwl` pair (old).
Fix: set Settings > World name to the exact name of the correct world (or edit `WORLD_NAME` in `/root/valheim.env` and recreate via the dashboard, not by hand, so the platform stays in sync), then confirm in the log that the intended world loaded. Before any change, copy the world folder: `cp -a /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local /root/worlds_local.$(date +%F-%H%M)`.
Tell the customer: which world is running now, that no world was deleted, what caused it, and that a rename always starts a new world.

#### Playbook 4: Mods not loading / "mod disappeared"

Checks:
- Server type must be `bepinex` (Settings). On `vanilla` nothing loads (2 of 4 live servers were vanilla on 2026-10-01).
- Folder layout: DLLs under `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/<Author-Mod>/` (BepInEx loads recursively). The image copies this folder into the live BepInEx dir at container start, so changes need a restart.
- `grep -i "loading \[" /opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/LogOutput.log` lists what actually loaded; compare with the folder.
- After a Valheim Steam update the loader can be reset: the files are intact but not loaded. Fix: restart the server (T11, twice in one day: a second update the same day required a second restart).
- Missing dependency (Jotunn, other BepInEx libs): log shows missing reference / type load exceptions. Install the dependency into its own plugin folder.
- Mods built for an older game build can crash or silently fail after 1.0 (T15 customer: "some mods might be for older versions").
- Packages with `patchers/`, `core/`, `monomod/` folders are refused by the one-click installer: the image does not sync those preloader folders from `/config`.
Fix: restart; install missing deps; remove incompatible mods; switch to `bepinex` type.
Tell the customer: the files are safe, a game update reset the loader, a restart reloads them; mention it can recur after the next Valheim update.

#### Playbook 5: Version / mod mismatch ("Incompatible version", join refused after a mod install)

Facts: a server marked modded requires every gameplay mod on every client at the same version (ValheimPlus case, T12). Server-only/cosmetic-free mods are fine without client install; client-side-only mods are not catalogued for servers.
Checks: list server plugins (`ls /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins`) and each manifest version (`cat .../<Mod>/manifest.json` where present); ask for the player's r2modman/Thunderstore profile export or screenshot. Also check the base game version: the game builds must match (the server self-updates only when idle; players may be a build ahead/behind after a patch day: A2S EDF keywords `g=1.0.xx` shows the server build).
Fix: align versions (players install the same mod versions) or remove the mod server-side (note that removal restarts the server). Install via the dashboard Mods tab where possible so versions are the newest and dependencies are included.
Tell the customer: the exact mod names/versions required on every PC, or that we removed the mod and they can join again.

#### Playbook 6: Console / admin / devcommands

Facts: vanilla Valheim never gives a remote admin cheat access on a real dedicated server (the gate `Terminal.IsCheatsEnabled()` is host-only), so `devcommands` fails even for admins. The third-party "Server devcommands" mod crashed on the current game build (HarmonyException in `Awake()`, 2026-09-09). Nxeon's own plugin (`NxeonDevAdmin`) does the one needed thing: lets a player in `adminlist.txt` use devcommands. It is mounted automatically on every `bepinex` server. It is NOT active on `vanilla` servers.
Steps for the customer: (1) server type = BepInEx (Settings; world is kept); (2) find their Steam64 ID (17 digits, steamid.io); (3) Files tab: edit `/opt/valheim/config/adminlist.txt` and add the ID **on its own line, with a trailing newline**; or enter it in Settings > "Admin SteamIDs" (`ADMINLIST_IDS`, space-separated; the image writes the file). (4) Restart the server; (5) join and press F5 to open the console, then `devcommands`.
Checks if it still fails: file ends with a newline and has no stray characters (LC4: a missing newline was found); `adminlist.txt` format accepted by the image is a bare SteamID64 per line (the Platform-prefixed `Steam_<id>` form appears in the 2026-09-20 notes: UNVERIFIED which the current image prefers, try the bare form first); `ls /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/nxeon-dev-admin` exists; `grep -i NxeonDevAdmin /opt/valheim/data/bepinex/BepInEx/LogOutput.log` shows it loaded; confirm the third-party "Server devcommands" mod is NOT installed alongside it (T-LC4: uninstall it). Achievements restore after the cheat-flag patch: each player runs the patch-note command individually (`yesiuseddevcommandsbutiwantmyachievementsanyway`); admin-list membership does not apply it server-wide (T4).
Server log is visible in the dashboard Console tab; there is no command box for Valheim.
Tell the customer: the steps above, and that being on the admin list grants console access only.

#### Playbook 7: Password rules

- Required, minimum 5 characters, must not be contained in the world name (Valheim refuses to start otherwise). Stored as `SERVER_PASS` in `/root/valheim.env`.
- Changing it recreates the container (restart). Tell players the new password.
- Historic: before 2026-09-08 every server shared the catalog default `changeme12` and the field was not visible. Any server older than that may still run it: check `grep SERVER_PASS /root/valheim.env` on old servers (UNVERIFIED how many remain) and recommend a change. Do not paste passwords into tickets.
- A "SSH password" is a different thing (VM login, Overview > SSH, "Reset password" button). T1 lost time to this confusion: confirm which one the customer means.

#### Playbook 8: Performance / memory / ballooning

- Valheim is mostly single-thread-bound; RAM scales with explored world and mods. Recommendation basis: `lib/game-player-recommend.ts` (about 410 MB per player over base: ESTIMATE, not measured).
- `free -m`; `docker stats --no-stream valheim`; compare to plan. 4 GB plan with ~23 mods booted and ran, but it is tight; recommend 8 GB for heavy mod lists or 20 players.
- Ballooning: new VMs get a balloon floor of 50% (`worker/index.ts` `balloonFloorMB`, min 1024); on a 4 GB plan that is 2048. On a busy node Proxmox can squeeze the guest to ~1.8 GB (`1.82 GiB is not enough memory` in the log, T8; confirmed again 2026-10-01). Fix: on the node `qm set <vmid> --balloon 0` and cold reboot (stop + start, not guest reboot-only). Verify with `free -m` inside the guest.
- High ping: region (Playbook in FAQ). Valheim tolerates up to ~100 ms (PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md); 276 ms from Philippines to Germany was the T1 case.
- Lag with BetterNetworking-type mods is normally an improvement; staff recommended it (T2).

#### Playbook 9: Crossplay / consoles

- Setting: Settings > Crossplay (`CROSSPLAY=true`). Before 2026-09-15 the setting was saved but never applied to the container (fixed in `applyValheim`); on older servers check `docker inspect valheim | grep CROSSPLAY` shows `CROSSPLAY=true`.
- Crossplay switches Steam matchmaking to PlayFab so Xbox / Microsoft Store (and, per the T6 outcome, PlayStation) clients can join. In T6 staff first said PlayStation is excluded, then the customer found an official statement and the PS5 player did join. Treat console support as supported when `CROSSPLAY=true`, and verify the current platform list against Iron Gate's current docs before promising a specific platform: UNVERIFIED.
- Consoles cannot type an IP. Console players find servers by NAME in the in-game server list; so the server must be listed (community/public listing) and the exact name given. Ask what exactly the console player enters (T6). Server name is `SERVER_NAME` (default "Nxeon" at provision; the Settings schema for Valheim has no server-name field: UNVERIFIED how the customer renames it today, see Section 7).
- A PC/Steam client joins crossplay servers by the same Join IP flow.

#### Playbook 10: Backups and restore

Three different things, do not mix them up:
1. **Image auto-backups (in-game world zips):** the `lloesche/valheim-server` image archives worlds to `/opt/valheim/config/backups/` (zip files, automatic, old ones pruned). Schedule/retention defaults are the image's own (README memory: hourly, ~3 days: UNVERIFIED, read `docker exec valheim env | grep BACKUP`). To restore one: stop the server (`docker stop valheim`), copy the current world folder aside, unzip the archive into `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/` (zips contain the world files), start, confirm in the log.
2. **Dashboard "Backups" tab / world backup job (`GAME_BACKUP`):** archives the located world dir to `/var/backups/nxeon-game/valheim-<timestamp>.tar.gz`. The directory search list for Valheim does not include `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local` (see Section 7): on current Docker-based servers this job may report "Could not locate the world/save directory": UNVERIFIED live, test before relying on it.
3. **VM backups (vzdump):** platform disaster recovery and the customer's "restore from backup" on the server page. A false identity alarm that left VMs powered off was fixed in `8f6066be2e` (confirm deployed). Until you have confirmed that, do restores by hand and tell the customer.
Always copy the live world folder before any restore: a world restore overwrites progress made since the backup (T3 lesson).

### 4. Mods guide

How installs work
- **One-click (Mods & Plugins tab / NX Labs catalog, ~1.2k Thunderstore Valheim packages):** `lib/mods/installers/valheim.ts`. Requires server type `bepinex` (else the panel says to switch in Settings; the world is kept). Resolves dependencies from the package's own declared list (max depth 6, max 40 packages), never installs BepInExPack (the image provides BepInEx), refuses packages needing `patchers/core/monomod`, skips `config/` defaults, places files in `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/<Author-Name>/`, records state, supports update/disable/enable/uninstall, then a restart is required to load. Catalog quality gate: non-deprecated, server-side capable, > 1,000 downloads (`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` NX Labs section).
- **Legacy path** (`worker/game-mods.ts` `installModReal`, unzips into `nxeon-<slug>/`) is only used if the engine path is off; the 2026-09-20 note that it never restarts the server applies to that path only.
- **Customer uploads (Files tab):** Thunderstore zips and loose DLLs into `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins/`.

The zip rule (verified 2026-10-01, T15 with 23 mods)
1. Thunderstore downloads often bundle several versions: extract **only the newest version**.
2. Put each mod in `plugins/<Author-Mod>/` (a plain DLL can sit loose or in its own folder).
3. **Never extract the BepInExPack zip**: the container already has BepInEx and a second copy breaks loading.
4. Restart afterwards and check `LogOutput.log` for the load lines.

Compatibility traps
- Client parity: gameplay mods must match on every client (Playbook 5). Server-side-only mods (e.g. MaxPlayerCount, BetterNetworking: UNVERIFIED whether each requires a client copy; BetterNetworking is normally installed on both sides, check its Thunderstore page) may not.
- Game updates (1.0 on 2026-09-09 and following patches) break old mods: ValheimPlus is deprecated; many older mod lists in customer zips were for pre-1.0 builds.
- Dependencies: Jotunn (`ValheimModding-Jotunn`) and similar BepInEx library mods must be present for content mods; the one-click installer adds declared dependencies, manual uploads do not.
- Do not combine "Server devcommands" (third-party, crashes on current build) with Nxeon's own NxeonDevAdmin.
- RCON mods exist (`rcon` by AviiNL, `Rcon Commands`): the possible route to real kick/ban is documented in the 2026-09-20 DOCUMENTATION entry and is untested.
- Memory expectations: 23 mods ran on the 4 GB plan but with a ~3 min boot and little headroom; per-player RAM estimate ~410 MB (`lib/game-player-recommend.ts`, estimate). Large mod lists or 20 players: 8 GB plan.
- A mod installed does restart the server (T2). Warn first.

### 5. World management

- **Format (Valheim 1.0):** each world is a folder `worlds_local/<WorldName>/` with `_main.N.db2`, `.fwl2`, and `.chunk` files. Older worlds are `<WorldName>.db` + `.fwl` (+ `_backup_*`). Upload/restore the folder intact; a partial copy (only the db2) will not load. Characters live on each player's PC, not the server.
- **Upload a world:** stop nothing needed if uploading a NEW name; upload folder to `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/`, set Settings > World name to the folder name. Overwriting the currently running world while the server runs is unsafe: stop the server first (staff did this by hand in T15, the customer first uploaded to `/opt/` and staff moved it).
- **Move to another region/node:** Section 6.
- **Backups:** Playbook 10.
- **Presets and modifiers:** Settings > World. `preset` plus per-modifier overrides (`deathpenalty`, `portals`, `raids`); overrides win over the preset. Equivalent to the in-game `-modifier deathpenalty casual -modifier portals casual` requested in LC4. Preset list: normal, casual, easy, hard, hardcore, immersive, hammer (creative). Changing any of them restarts the server; the world data is not reset by modifiers.
- **Seed/new world:** a new world name generates a new world; the old files stay.

### 6. Operations / admin cheat-sheet

Where things are in /admin
- Game servers: `/admin/games`. Server detail/Ops console: `/admin/ops` (diagnose, IP ops, fleet ops, job queue, customer ops). Tickets/chats: admin support area. Community (free) servers: `/admin/free-servers` (area `fleet`). NX Labs: `/admin/nxlabs`.
- Worker jobs relevant to Valheim (systemd `nxeon-worker`; do not restart it): `PROVISION`, `GAME_POWER`, `GAME_CONFIG_APPLY` (settings -> container recreate), `GAME_MOD_SYNC`, `GAME_BACKUP`, `GAME_REINSTALL`, `GAME_UPDATE`, `SYNC_FORWARDS`, `BACKUP_RESTORE`, plus the ~60 s log player-tracking sweep (`logPlayerTrackingSweep`). Job names as seen in code (`lib/actions-game-control.ts`, `worker/index.ts`): check the Ops job queue for exact current types.
- Power start window: 180 s for Valheim (`powerStartTimeoutMs`); UI start grace is 6 min (`lib/game-runtime.ts`).

Moving a server between regions/nodes (T1, T15; staff-run, 30-45 min downtime)
1. Tell the customer the downtime and get consent; ask for any newer world folder (upload to the Files tab or a zip). Do not start the move until the world files are in.
2. Re-provision the same plan on the target node (brand-new VMID, never reuse one, check all 5 nodes; Singapore may need a new node first).
3. Restore world files into `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local/` on the new VM (whole folder), copy `adminlist.txt` and the plugins folder, and carry over `/root/valheim.env` values (SERVER_PASS, WORLD_NAME, BEPINEX, CROSSPLAY, SERVER_ARGS) so the password and world stay the same. In T15 the SSH password was not carried over: tell the customer to press "Reset password" if SSH login fails.
4. Verify: log has `Game server connected`, A2S answers on N+1, ports are consecutive (Playbook 1 step 5). Then give the new address (the port changes!) and retire the old VM per policy.
5. Update customer: new `IP:port`, same server password, world loaded.

Gotchas to check on every move or reboot
- **Consecutive port block:** the allocator hands out one public port per rule, so N, N+1, N+2 are not guaranteed (Section 7).
- **Ballooning:** `qm set <vmid> --balloon 0` + cold reboot on 4 GB plans if the guest sees ~1.8 GB.
- **Hairpin/firewall** and node NAT: a VM cannot reach nxeon.cloud unless the firewall hairpin fix is in place (separate entry in this document).
- Never experiment on the customer's live container; copy files first.

Free public Valheim server (dormant until owner action)
- Plan, abuse model and runbook: `docs/PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md`. One shared server, password published and rotated weekly, unlisted (`SERVER_PUBLIC=0`), daily backups kept 7 days, memory limit 4 GB / 2 CPU. Installer and day-2 tool inside the VM: `scripts/provision-public-valheim.sh` (`install`, `status`, `rotate-password`, `backup-now`, `ban`, `update`, `health`). Platform probe: `scripts/probe-free-public-servers.ts`. Marketing page `/free-valheim-server` 404s unless a row is LIVE. The script has never been run on a real VM and its image cron variable names are from memory of the README (UNVERIFIED); confirm in `docker logs` on first boot.

### 7. Known issues and open to-dos

| Ballooning floor | `balloonFloorMB` = 50% of plan RAM, min 1024. On 4 GB plans a busy node squeezes the guest to ~1.8 GB. To do: no balloon (or higher floor) for game plans; existing VMs need `--balloon 0` + cold reboot by hand. |

World listing and `GAME_BACKUP` for Valheim probably find nothing. Code gap, not fixed here. |

### 8. Customer reply templates

Keep them short, no internal jargon, no provider names, no invented timings. Replace `<...>`. Never send a ticket reply without the owner's sign-off rule for this team being met.

1. **Can't connect (first reply)**
   "Thanks for flagging this. Your server is running on our side. Please join with <ip>:<port> (Join by IP) and the server password from your Settings tab, and restart your Valheim game before trying again, as that clears a cached failed connection. If it still fails, send us a screenshot of the Join box with the error, and the list of mods you have installed on your PC, and we'll dig in right away."

2. **Version mismatch / mod parity**
   "Valheim only lets players in when their mods match the server exactly. Your server runs: <mod list with versions>. Every player needs the same mods at the same versions. If you'd rather not ask everyone to install them, tell us and we'll remove the mod on the server so everyone can join again. Note that adding or removing a mod restarts the server for a minute or two."

3. **Mod disappeared after a game update**
   "A Valheim update reset the mod loader on your server. Your mod files are safe, the server just needs a restart to load them again. Shall we restart now? Players online will be disconnected briefly. This can happen again after the next Valheim update, and a restart fixes it each time."

4. **World missing / switched**
   "We checked your server directly. Your world files are all still saved. The server was loading <current world>, and your <other world> is also still on disk. Tell us which one holds the progress you want and we'll switch to it safely, after taking a copy of both first. We won't change anything until you confirm."

5. **Admin / console access**
   "To use the in-game console: 1) Find your Steam64 ID (17 digits, steamid.io shows it from your profile link). 2) In your server's Files tab open /opt/valheim/config/adminlist.txt and add the ID on its own line, then save. 3) Restart the server from the dashboard. 4) Join and press F5. Your server already has our own dev-commands support, so you don't need to install a separate mod. Being on the admin list gives console access; achievements fixes must be run by each player."

6. **Password**
   "Your join password is in Settings > Server password. You can change it there: it needs at least 5 characters and can't be part of your world name. Saving restarts the server for a moment, so let your players know the new password."

7. **Upload my world / my mods**
   "Open your server's Files tab. Worlds go in /opt/valheim/config/worlds_local (upload the whole world folder, not just one file), then set the World name in Settings to the folder name. Mods go in /opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins, and your server type must be BepInEx. If you have zip files, upload them and tell us, and we'll unpack them for you. Use only the newest version of each mod and skip the BepInEx pack, as your server already includes it."

8. **Move to another region**
   "We can move your server to <region>. Expect up to 30-45 minutes of downtime, your world and password carry over, and the address and port will change: we'll send you the new one as soon as it's up. If you have a newer copy of your world on your own PC, upload it to the Files tab first so we move the latest progress. Shall we start now?"

9. **High ping**
   "High ping usually comes from distance between you and the server. Your server is in <region>; players in <area> usually get a better connection from <closer region>. We can move it for you (up to 30-45 minutes of downtime, world kept). Would you like that?"

10. **Crossplay / console players**
   "Crossplay is switched on for your server. Console players can't type an IP address, so they find the server by name in Valheim's in-game server list: ask them to search for exactly '<server name>'. PC players can keep joining by IP. If someone still can't find it, tell us the platform and what they see, and we'll investigate."

### How to keep this current

- Add a line to this section the same day a Valheim ticket teaches something new; cite the ticket/date and mark anything unchecked as **UNVERIFIED** until proven.
- When a game patch day breaks something (1.0 on 2026-09-09 did), add the symptom to Playbooks 3-5.
- Re-read `lib/game-config.ts` VALHEIM schema, `lib/games.ts` ports and `GamePlan` rows before quoting fields, ports or prices; update Section 1 if they change.
- Close the Section 7 rows as fixes ship (port allocator, ballooning, `dataRoots`, server-name field) and confirm the file-manager extract/folder-upload deployment.
- The AI chat agent source: mirror changes into `lib/kb-plans.ts` / the chat knowledge base after editing this section.

Branch `docs/valheim-knowledge-base`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-valheimkb`, commit `6721a0ad44`. It changes only `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`: 291 lines appended, no other section touched, no code changes. The auto-push hook was not checked. Notes are in `/root/agent-notes/valheimkb.md`. Verification was a read-through plus spot-checks of ports, job names, schema field names and plan sizes against the source and read-only prod DB; nothing was built or run.

**What the KB contains.** New top-level section "Knowledge base: Valheim", placed last.
1. Orientation table covering plans, ports, paths, how the server runs, the settings schema and the Nxeon dev-commands plugin.
2. Customer FAQ, about 20 answers, each tagged with its source ticket or chat.
3. Ten playbooks (symptom, checks with commands, fix, what to tell the customer):
   - can't connect
   - crashes
   - world missing/switched (the 2026-09-11 incident)
   - mods disappeared
   - version mismatch
   - console/admin
   - password
   - memory/ballooning
   - crossplay
   - backups/restore
4. Mods guide, including the Thunderstore zip rule.
5. World management.
6. Admin cheat-sheet: server-move procedure and the free public Valheim server.
7. Known issues table.
8. Ten reply templates, plus "How to keep this current".

The existing "can't connect" runbook is kept and Playbook 1 folds its checklist in. I wrote the section directly, with no separate review pass.

**Verified against code or prod DB.**
- **Plans:** only two live Valheim plans exist in prod: 4 GB / 2 vCPU / 30 GB / 10 players and 8 GB / 3 vCPU / 50 GB / 20 players. List prices are 1438 and 2446 cents; intro prices are 999 and 1699. The 2 GB and 12 GB plans in `seed-gameplans-4tier.ts` are not in the DB.
- **Ports, paths, mounts, container and image:** UDP 2456-2458, container `valheim`, image `lloesche/valheim-server`, the `/opt/valheim/config` and `/opt/valheim/data` mounts, and the plugin folder.
- **Settings fields and values:** all match `lib/game-config.ts`.
- **Other:** the 180 s power-start timeout, the A2S port being the game port + 1, and the log-based player tracking.
- **File manager:** extract-archives (`ca30a05922`) and folder-upload (`a6201db7ed`) are both ancestors of main.
- **World fixes:** the world-switch and restore-false-alarm fix (`8f6066be2e`) is on main.

**UNVERIFIED, and labelled as such in the KB.**
- Whether the extract, folder-upload and world-switch fixes are deployed to prod.
- Renewal price semantics for the two Valheim plans.
- The image's auto-backup schedule and retention; the README default I recalled is hourly, about 3 days.
- Whether `adminlist.txt` takes the bare SteamID64 or the `Steam_<id>` form, and whether edits apply without a restart.
- Whether the current game build supports crossplay for PlayStation. The T6 ticket contradicts itself, so the KB says to check Iron Gate's current docs.
- Whether MaxPlayerCount or BetterNetworking need a client-side copy.
- How a customer renames a server today.
- Whether the "terraheim" world-creation crash is really a game-engine bug.
- How many pre-2026-09-08 servers still use the default password `changeme12`.
- The free-Valheim installer's cron variable names, and whether it works at all (never run on a real VM).
- Whether `GAME_BACKUP` works for Valheim (see the `dataRoots` gap below).

**Code bugs and gaps found (not fixed).**
1. **`dataRoots` miss the real world folder.** `lib/game-control.ts` `GAME_CONTROL.valheim.dataRoots` lists the unity3d paths and `/opt/valheim/worlds_local`, but not `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local`. The world listing and the `GAME_BACKUP` job (`worker/game-control.ts` `createWorldBackup`) will probably report "Could not locate the world/save directory" on Docker-based servers.
2. **No Valheim server-name setting.** The schema has no `SERVER_NAME` field and provisioning hardcodes 'Nxeon'. Console players find servers by name, so this matters.
3. **Public ports are allocated one at a time** (`allocateGameForward` in `worker/index.ts`), so N, N+1, N+2 are not guaranteed.
4. **The balloon floor is 50% of plan RAM, minimum 1024** (`worker/index.ts` `balloonFloorMB`). On 4 GB plans that is 2048, which squeezed the Jay case guest to about 1.8 GB.
5. **The chat bot denies the 4 GB Valheim plan.** `lib/kb-plans.ts` lists only the 8 GB plan, and the bot told customers there was no 4 GB tier twice.
6. **Checkout hid the required `SERVER_PASS` field on 2026-09-16.** I did not find the root cause or confirm the current state.
7. **`docs/PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md` quotes list prices of 14.38 and 24.46 dollars.** The advertised prices are 9.99 and 16.99 dollars, so the plan doc is easy to misread.
8. **Valheim has no kick/ban from the panel, and leave times are inferred.** There is no native RCON, and the `<id>` in the join log is a ZDOID, not a SteamID64.

content.text:
I've appended a "Knowledge base: Valheim" section to the end of `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`. It is committed on `docs/valheim-knowledge-base` (commit `6721a0ad44`, worktree `/opt/nxeon-wt-valheimkb`). It is 291 lines, a bit under your 400-700 target. I checked ports, job names, settings field names and plan sizes against the source and the read-only prod DB. Nothing was built or run.

It follows your structure: orientation, customer FAQ, ten playbooks, mods guide, world management, ops cheat-sheet, known issues, ten reply templates and a "keep this current" note. The existing "can't connect" runbook is kept, and Playbook 1 folds its checklist in. I wrote it directly with no separate review pass.

The statements I could not verify from code, tickets or live checks are labelled UNVERIFIED in the section. The main ones:
- Whether the file-manager extract and folder-upload features, and the world-switch/restore fix (`8f6066be2e`), are deployed to prod. All three are merged to main.
- The image's auto-backup schedule and retention.
- Whether `adminlist.txt` takes a bare SteamID64 or the `Steam_<id>` form.
- Which platforms Valheim crossplay currently covers, since the PS5 ticket contradicts itself.
- Whether MaxPlayerCount and BetterNetworking need a client-side copy.
- How many old servers still use the shared default password `changeme12`.
- Whether the free-Valheim installer script works, since it has never run on a real VM.

I noticed these code gaps while researching and did not fix them:
- **World folder path:** the Valheim `dataRoots` in `lib/game-control.ts` don't include `/opt/valheim/config/worlds_local`. The world listing and `GAME_BACKUP` job will probably find nothing on Docker-based servers.
- **Server name:** there is no Valheim server-name setting. Provisioning hardcodes 'Nxeon', which matters because consoles find servers by name.
- **Port allocator:** public ports are allocated one at a time, so N, N+1, N+2 aren't guaranteed.
- **Ballooning:** the floor is 50% of plan RAM. On 4 GB plans that is 2048, which squeezed the Jay case guest to about 1.8 GB.
- **Chat bot:** `lib/kb-plans.ts` lists only the 8 GB Valheim plan, so the bot twice told customers there was no 4 GB tier.
- **Checkout:** the required password field was missing from a Valheim order on 2026-09-16. I did not find the root cause or confirm the current state.
- **Free-Valheim plan doc:** `docs/PLAN-FREE-VALHEIM.md` quotes list prices of 14.38 and 24.46 dollars, not the advertised 9.99 and 16.99, so it is easy to misread.
- **Kick/ban:** there is no kick or ban from the panel, and player leave times are inferred.

The notes file is `/root/agent-notes/valheimkb.md`.
